derivation_review: Ex-ante mandate/benchmark, supplementary factor comparator and peer population are different defined questions. Active mean is not relabeled alpha or skill. The closed-market aggregate active/passive identity uses beginning-dollar weights, a complete universe and an explicit conditional net-cost ordering.

Tracking-error sample variance uses n-1 and the active differential; Sharpe uses the period-specific cash differential. Variance decomposition includes active-benchmark covariance. Zero denominators return undefined, and scale invariance does not imply unlimited implementation.

The additive-horizon variance derivation counts h diagonal terms and 2(h-k) covariance pairs at lag k. Square-root scaling requires stable moments and zero serial covariances; it is not exact compounded-return risk. The t=IR*sqrt(n) identity is separated from valid sampling inference.

OLS intercept, slopes and the active-mean decomposition follow from full-rank normal equations with an intercept. The disclosed synthetic factor construction is not a pricing model. Observed factor means and explanatory fit do not establish premiums or skill.

Constant beginning-NAV fees shift means/intercepts and preserve centered moments and residuals. Classic fixed-design coefficient variance is derived from the linear estimator with covariance sigma-squared I; residual degrees of freedom and unvalidated normal-reference/selection assumptions are explicit.

Single-period allocation/selection/interaction identity proved by expansion and the zero sum of active weights. Alternative grouping, zero-sector-return boundaries, intraperiod trading and causal limitations are explained.

Multiperiod product difference is proved by telescoping hybrid portfolio/benchmark wealth. The exact chronological link is disclosed and its component order dependence demonstrated; arithmetic summation, compounding active differences and relative terminal wealth are distinct quantities.

Fee and contribution ordering is explicit. The fund and benchmark receive the same contribution after month 4 return and fee. TWR and MWR have different bases. Positive initial capital and nonnegative intervening contributions give a strictly increasing terminal-value polynomial and unique positive gross MWR root.

Panel includes all entrants/exits and complete terminal payouts. Initial cohort is fixed at date 0, ranking uses only Y1-Y2, and holdout allocations are frozen before Y3. Selected closure proceeds stay in zero-return cash. Dynamic all-available rebalancing and hindsight survivor filtering are separate strategies.

Top-set permutation reference assumes exchangeability rather than inferring it. Small-sample persistence, selected intervals and regression coefficients are not presented as statistical or prospective skill findings. Decision criteria include actual mandate, costs, capacity and independent evidence.
